strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 datasets with multiple downstream tasks and systematic scaling analysis demonstrating rigor and thoroughness
Novel and well-motivated flat map representation elegantly bridges spatial detail and computational efficiency, showing empirical advantages over volume and parcellation approaches
Strong reproducibility and transparency: open-source code, detailed implementation details, BRAINMARKS benchmark creation, and honest discussion of limitations and failures
Practical significance as first systematic study of fMRI foundation models with proper scaling laws and benchmarking, creating valuable resources for the neuroscience-ML community
Clear presentation with informative visualizations, comprehensive tables, and logical progression from method through experiments to analysis
Honest reporting of inconsistent results across datasets and when foundation models underperform simpler baselines, strengthening credibility
Computational efficiency gains demonstrated (2.5× speedup vs volume models) with detailed cost analysis provided
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: straightforward application of standard masked autoencoders and Vision Transformers with primary innovation being the representation choice, which while sensible is somewhat incremental

Inconsistent and modest empirical improvements with model ranking varying across datasets and improvements often within confidence intervals; on some datasets (COCO24) foundation models barely exceed simple connectome baseline

Poor out-of-distribution generalization with significant performance drops on NSD/COCO24 despite HCP-YA pretraining, and model improvements varying by pretraining dataset; applicability to real-world clinical settings unclear

Critical findings inadequately explained: coordinate normalization improves training but hurts test performance (Table 15), data augmentation provides no benefit (Table 9), and input normalization choice dramatically affects results—suggesting hyperparameter sensitivity rather than fundamental insights

Data augmentation failure (Table 9) unexplored; the lack of improvement from TR scaling, aspect jittering, and intensity augmentation raises questions about whether models learn robust vs. dataset-specific features
Limited mechanistic understanding of why flat maps work: empirical advantage over volume/parcellation shown but the geometric or representational properties exploited by MAE not analyzed
Benchmark scope limitations: small sample sizes (minimum 16 subjects), limited acquisition diversity, no cross-site generalization analysis, and state prediction tasks underrepresented
Scaling behavior shows diminishing returns (power-law in Fig 7) and saturation around 50K parameters; unclear if massive pretraining investment justifies computational cost (~7K H100 hours)
Ethical considerations underexplored: implications of large-scale fMRI models for cognitive/emotional state inference and clinical deployment risks deserve deeper treatment
Dense presentation with important findings (e.g., pretraining dataset selection matters more than size) buried; main narrative could clearer state when and why foundation models help
